description: This line plot illustrates the similarity of Hidden State Alignments (HSAs) across different language pairs as a function of model layer depth in the Qwen1.5-1.8B architecture. The x-axis, labeled “Layer,” spans from 0 to 22 with integer tick marks, indicating discrete transformer layers. The y-axis, labeled “Similarity,” ranges from 0.00 to 0.45 in increments of 0.05, representing the computed similarity metric. Four distinct lines correspond to language pair comparisons: “en&en” (red solid line), “en&es” (blue solid line), “en&el” (green solid line), and “en&bn” (magenta solid line). All lines begin near the bottom of the y-axis (approximately 0.04–0.07 at Layer 0), rise to a peak around Layer 6 (with “en&en” reaching ~0.27 and “en&es” ~0.25), then generally decline until Layer 20–21, where they dip to their lowest values (~0.05–0.08). From Layer 22 onward, all lines exhibit a sharp, steep increase, with “en&en” surging to ~0.44, “en&es” to ~0.27, “en&el” to ~0.30, and “en&bn” to ~0.30, indicating a pronounced late-layer similarity boost across all language pairs.
